conviction_note: The evidence points both ways. Credit keeps improving (company July/August NCO 4.7%/4.9% against 5.1%/5.1% a year earlier, and the September trust NCO 3.86% against 4.21%), and the full-year guide implies a Q3 of about $2.55-2.69 against a $2.48 consensus. Against that, peers built reserves on the macro outlook after the 16 September Fed hike, partner payments are rising with better credit, and this name sold 6 of its last 8 prints, including a $0.50 beat with a raised guide in Q2 (-1.63%). So p_up is 49 on a 4.0% absolute move, and the findings sum to about zero. The two measurements agree: neither has a sign.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS consensus $2.48 (Earnings Whispers, whisper $2.53, https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/syf; Barchart's 6-estimate figure is also $2.48, but it came through search only because the page did not load, https://www.barchart.com/story/news/3720012/do-wall-street-analysts-like-synchrony-financial-stock). Other sources are lower: TickerLeague $2.43 (https://tickerleague.com/companies/SYF/estimates) and Benzinga $2.35. The company's FY2026 EPS guide of $9.25-9.50 (Q2 call, https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-synchrony-financial-stock/) less H1 actuals of $4.86 ($2.27 + $2.59) implies H2 $4.39-4.64. My print estimate is about $2.60, which is +5% against $2.48.
positioning_check: Short interest at the 2026-09-30 settlement was 17.45M shares, 5.4% of shares outstanding, with 5.67 days to cover (2026-09-15: 18.82M, 6.89 days; trending down from 22.9M in May) per https://equibles.com/stocks/syf/shortinterest. That is moderate, not a crowded short. The baseline's 25-delta skew is +5.96 vol points (downside paid) and the put/call OI ratio is 1.95, but total OI is only 3,108 and the ATM spread is 44% of mid, so the option read is indicative. The stock is 17% below its 52-week high and -2.1% over 20 days. Its own print history is 6 of 8 down, median absolute move 1.69%, maximum 5.82%. One caveat: the 2026-08-14 baseline row is the monthly credit-stats 8-K (item 2.02, filed 2026-08-17), not an earnings print.

findings.finding: Q3 credit is tracking clearly better year on year. The company's monthly 8-Ks show NCO of 4.7% (July) and 4.9% (August) against 5.1%/5.1% a year earlier, and 30+ delinquency of 4.2% against 4.3%. The September Synchrony Card Issuance Trust 10-D (filed 2026-10-15) shows NCO of 3.86% against 4.21% in September 2025 (3-month average 4.05% against 4.36%) and 30+ delinquency of 2.88% of receivables against 2.93%. Q3 NCO is therefore near 4.85% against 5.16% in Q3 2025 and 5.43% in Q2. Full-year NCO tracks near 5.2-5.3% against a guide of 'below 5.5%', which leaves room to tighten the NCO guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NCO also improved year on year in Q2 2026 (5.43% against 5.70%), and the stock fell 1.63% on the print. Credit improvement has not been paid on recent prints.
findings.why_not_priced: July and August are public 8-Ks and consensus models them. The September trust report is a 10-D that few equity readers open, and it is the only company-level September credit datapoint before the print. If it were priced, the 25-delta skew would not still be paying 6 vol points for downside on a name whose loss rate is falling about 30bp year on year. The finding also lands inside an already-guided NCO ceiling, which is why it is small.
findings.independence: The company's monthly 8-K for the 13 months to August 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001601712/000160171226000037/creditstatsfinancialtables.htm) is a separate document. Citi's Q3 release (2026-10-13) says USCC NCOs fell 4%, 'mainly from improved credit performance in private label cards' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000831001/000110465926115323/c-ex99d1.htm). Bread Financial's August loss rate was 6.40% against 7.57%.

findings.finding: Card peers that reported after Synchrony last spoke built reserves on the macro outlook, not on credit. Citi's U.S. Consumer Cards booked a $208M net reserve build in Q3 2026, 'driven mainly by changes in the macroeconomic outlook', even as its NCOs fell 4%. JPMorgan built $539M firmwide. Both followed the 16 September 2026 Fed hike to 3.75-4.00%, and Synchrony's July guide assumed no rate change. A macro overlay in Synchrony's CECL could push Q3 provision above the growth-driven build consensus carries (Wenzel: the reserve rate 'probably doesn't really moderate from here').
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 a smaller reserve release ($163M against $265M) raised the provision; EPS still beat and the stock fell 1.63%. Q4 2025 had a reserve build of about $75M and the stock fell 5.82% (with the rate-cap overhang that month).
findings.why_not_priced: Synchrony consensus was largely set around the July guide and the monthly credit data. The macro-driven reserve builds at Citi and JPMorgan came on 13-14 October, after Synchrony's 14 September Barclays appearance. If a macro build were in Synchrony's number, the Q3 EPS estimate would sit visibly below the guide-implied seasonal path. Instead it sits slightly below it. This is a proxy: Synchrony has not confirmed it.
findings.independence: JPMorgan's firmwide $539M Q3 build and the 16 September hike come from a different source (https://www.heygotrade.com/en/market-outlook/bank-stocks-q3-2026-earnings/, dated 2026-10-15). That source also shows JPMorgan's total provision fell year on year, which cuts against a large overlay. Partly offset by finding 1.

findings.finding: Citi's U.S. Consumer Cards non-interest revenue fell 62% year on year to -$758M in Q3 2026 on 'higher partner payment accruals and rewards costs'. That points to retailer share arrangements (Synchrony's RSAs) rising as private-label credit improves. Synchrony guided RSAs higher but within 4.0-4.5% of average receivables, so the credit benefit in finding 1 is partly paid away to partners.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history of an RSA surprise moving SYF alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Synchrony guided RSAs higher, so this is mostly expected and is sized close to zero. It would only matter if RSAs reach the top of the 4.0-4.5% band.
findings.independence: Same Citi document as finding 2. These are two different line items read once each, not one fact counted twice. The RSA guidance comes from the Q2 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-synchrony-financial-stock/).

findings.finding: Loan growth is accelerating but trails the year-end target. Period-end receivables were $103.0B in August 2026 against $100.2B a year earlier (+2.8%; June +2.0%, July +2.3%). The guide of 'mid-single-digit ending receivable growth by year-end' needs about $108B by December against $103.8B in December 2025, i.e. +$5-6B from August against +$3.6B over the same months of 2025. Meanwhile the trust's September payment rate was 24.5% against 23.1% a year earlier, and higher payments slow balance growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loan growth has been the soft line for two years (Q2 2026 +2%). The stock has drifted on it rather than gapped.
findings.why_not_priced: The month-by-month arithmetic against the year-end target is rarely spelled out in previews. Sized small because Wenzel reaffirmed mid-single-digit growth on 14 September with the August data in hand (Quartr summary, unverified), and the Walmart/OnePay ramp is the stated bridge. That reaffirmation is the counterweight and is already netted into the size.
findings.independence: The trust 10-D payment rate (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1724786/000110465926115929/tm2627192d1_ex99-1.htm) supports it. The Barclays conference summary (https://quartr.com/events/synchrony-financial-syf-barclays-24th-annual-global-financial-services-conference_3Yc546L6) cuts against it.

findings.finding: The full-year guide implies a Q3 above consensus. H1 2026 EPS was $4.86 ($2.27 + $2.59), so FY $9.25-9.50 implies H2 $4.39-4.64. On last year's split (Q3 was $2.86 of an H2 of $4.90, 58%), Q3 2026 comes to about $2.55-2.69 against a consensus of $2.35-2.48. A Q3 near $2.60 with a seasonal Q4 near $2.05 puts the year at or above the top of the guide, which makes a raise or narrowing toward the top likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats and raises have been sold. Q2 2026: $2.59 against about $2.09 with a raised guide, -1.63%. Q3 2025: $2.86, well above estimates, -0.71%. Q1 2025 and Q2 2025 beats: +2.82% and +1.76%.
findings.why_not_priced: The street sits at or below the guide-implied seasonal path despite Synchrony beating by about $0.50 last quarter. If it had priced a raise, the stock would not be 17% off its high with downside skew paid. Sized small anyway, because this name has not paid for beats.
findings.independence: The Q2 release confirms the $2.59 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001601712/000160171226000030/earningsrelease2q26.htm). The guide range comes from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-synchrony-financial-stock/). The whisper is $2.53 against $2.48 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/syf).

findings.finding: At the Barclays conference on 14 September 2026, CFO Wenzel said high-single-digit purchase volume growth was continuing, delinquency entry rates were better than pre-pandemic, NCOs were below the 5.5-6% long-term framework, and the loan target held. Q2 purchase volume was a record $49.8B (+8%), and Q3 2025's base was $46.0B. This comes from a third-party summary and is unverified against a transcript.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Record purchase volume in Q2 2026 (+8%) did not stop a -1.63% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, because it was said in public. Sized small. It matters as a mid-quarter read that the volume line is not deteriorating into the print.
findings.independence: Citi reported U.S. card spend +11% and JPMorgan card sales volume +10% in Q3 2026 (https://www.pymnts.com/?p=4306652).

outside_window.finding: American Express reports Q3 2026 on 2026-10-23 and Bread Financial's September performance update is typically late October. Both are card read-throughs, and both land after this window.
The FINRA short-interest settlement for 2026-10-15 publishes on about 2026-10-26.

searched_and_found_nothing: Synchrony 8-Ks after 2026-09-14: no September monthly credit 8-K (normally folded into the Q3 release); no 8.01 or 5.02 items since July
Partner wins or losses in September-October 2026 (Walmart/OnePay, Amazon, Lowe's): nothing dated in the window
Status of a credit card rate cap or late-fee rule in October 2026: only January 2026 coverage found (SYF -8.4% that day); no fresh legislative action surfaced
Analyst rating or target changes in October 2026: the latest found were July-August (UBS Hold $87 on 2026-08-03)
Q2 2026 10-Q interest-rate sensitivity table: not reachable in the fetched excerpt

rejected_candidates.candidate: The 16 September 2026 Fed hike filed as its own NII finding, since Synchrony's guide assumed no rate change
rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into finding 2 (macro reserve overlay). Its NII sign for Synchrony is ambiguous (prime-linked yields against lagging deposit repricing), and two weeks of Q3 exposure is negligible.

rejected_candidates.candidate: JPMorgan reported its card NCO falling to 2.91% from 3.15% a year earlier, with the September master trust NCO at 1.52% against 1.66%
rejected_candidates.detail: Industry credit improvement already carried by finding 1, which rests on Synchrony's own trust and monthly data.

rejected_candidates.candidate: An American Banker article reporting JPMorgan's card NCOs up 40% with credit 'normalization'
rejected_candidates.detail: The article is dated 2024-10-11 (Q3 2024), not 2026. The Q3 2026 data (PYMNTS 2026-10-13) shows card NCO falling.

baseline_tension: The fundamental read (improving credit, a guide-implied beat) cuts against the downside skew and the sold-beat history; the peer macro reserve builds agree with the skew. With the two balanced, p_up sits at 49 rather than leaning long.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the guide-implied beat finding went from +0.5 to +0.3, because this name sold a $0.50 beat with a raised guide in Q2 (-1.63%).
Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a proxy): the peer macro reserve-build finding went from -0.6 to -0.5, since Synchrony has not confirmed it.
Rule 6 (verify the bar): consensus sources disagree ($2.35-2.48), so the bar is anchored to two agreeing $2.48 sources plus the company guide arithmetic, and every finding stays small.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest checked before filing the negatives (5.4%, 5.7 days to cover, not crowded); the negatives agree with the skew, so no further cut.
Left standing: the credit, RSA, loan-growth and purchase-volume findings, and abs_move_pct and p_up.
